B1:
Touched fires many times per step, once for each body part (feet, legs) and again during physics contacts. Every event runs in the same frame before Destroy takes effect, so several handlers add 10 before the part is gone. Fix: add a debounce flag set synchronously before you award, and disconnect.
```lua
local part = script.Parent
local claimed = false
local conn
conn = part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
  if claimed then return end
  local plr = game.Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)
  if not plr then return end
  claimed = true
  conn:Disconnect()
  plr.leaderstats.Coins.Value += 10
  part:Destroy()
end)
```
For respawning coins, use a per-player cooldown table instead of a destroy.
B2: With StreamingEnabled, the client only has parts near the player; distant Models are not replicated or are streamed out. Indexing workspace.Map.Buildings.Hotel.Door with dots fails when Door (or Hotel) is not streamed in, and it can also stream out later. Fix 1: wait for it, for example local door = workspace.Map.Buildings:WaitForChild('Hotel'):WaitForChild('Door'), and set the Hotel or Door model's ModelStreamingMode = Atomic (or Persistent if it is small and must always exist), handling a nil result from a timeout. Fix 2 (better at scale): tag doors with CollectionService ('Door'). Connect through CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal('Door') plus GetTagged for existing doors, and disconnect on GetInstanceRemovedSignal, so doors are wired whenever they stream in or out. Better still, detect door touches on the server.
B3: Bugs: (1) The player can be nil after leaving, so plr.UserId errors inside pcall. The pcall fails, but the handler still returns PurchaseGranted, so the player is charged and gets nothing. (2) The pcall result is ignored, so a failed save is still reported as granted. (3) There is no PurchaseId record, so retries or re-runs grant again (double coins). (4) GetAsync followed by SetAsync is a non-atomic read-modify-write; concurrent server writes or a session's autosave can overwrite or duplicate. (5) It writes the DataStore directly while the live session profile may later overwrite it. Correct behavior: use one handler; return NotProcessedYet if the player or their profile is not ready, or on any error. Use UpdateAsync on the player's key, and if info.PurchaseId is already in the receipts list, return the data unchanged; otherwise add 100 and record the PurchaseId in the same update. Return PurchaseGranted only after the save succeeds. Keep the receipts list bounded.
B4: Remote arguments are serialized. Tables lose their metatables (and functions are not sent), so w arrives as a plain table {Name, Ammo} with no __index, and w:Fire() is nil. Instances only replicate as references if the client can see them; ServerStorage is never replicated, so the Muzzle arrives as nil. Fix: send plain data (an id or a state table) and rebuild the object on the client with a shared ModuleScript class in ReplicatedStorage: local w = Weapon.new(data). Put instances the client needs in ReplicatedStorage or Workspace, or send an identifier and let the client clone its own copy from ReplicatedStorage.
B5:
workspace:Raycast's second argument is the direction vector, and its length is the ray's range. .Unit makes it 1 stud long, so the ray only travels 1 stud. Also, if the origin is inside the shooter's own character, it hits that. Fix:
```lua
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {shooterCharacter}
local dir = (target - origin).Unit * 500 -- max range
local r = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
if r then print(r.Instance, r.Position) end
```
B6: When the last player leaves, the server shuts down. PlayerRemoving may fire, but the process closes before the yielding SetAsync finishes, so the save is cut off. Fix: use game:BindToClose to save every remaining player in parallel (task.spawn per player, wait for all to finish or about 25 s; the engine allows 30 s), sharing the same save function as PlayerRemoving, with a per-player saving flag so they don't double-save. Use UpdateAsync with retries, add periodic autosave (60-180 s, staggered) so a crash loses little, and skip the long wait in Studio.
B7:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local remote = game.ReplicatedStorage.Remotes.UseAbility
local COOLDOWN = 2
local lastUse = {} :: {[Player]: number}
remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, abilityId)
  if typeof(abilityId) ~= 'string' or not Abilities[abilityId] then return end
  local now = os.clock()
  local last = lastUse[player]
  if last and now - last < COOLDOWN then return end -- spam ignored silently
  local char = player.Character
  local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
  if not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
  lastUse[player] = now
  Abilities[abilityId](player, char)
end)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player) lastUse[player] = nil end)
```
The cooldown is server-authoritative (os.clock) and set before running the ability. The table entry is cleared on leave, so nothing leaks.

```lua
local MPS = game:GetService('MarketplaceService')
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local store = game:GetService('DataStoreService'):GetDataStore('PlayerData')
local GEMS100 = 123456
local handlers = {[GEMS100] = function(d) d.Gems = (d.Gems or 0) + 100 end}

  if not grant then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end

  if not player then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end -- retried on next join

  end)
```

In a session-locked system, apply the grant and receipt to the locked profile and save it, then return Granted. Only one script may set ProcessReceipt.
B9:
```lua
local TweenService = game:GetService('TweenService')
local info = TweenInfo.new(0.4, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
local OPEN, CLOSED = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, 0), UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1.5, 0)
local current
local function open()
  if current then current:Cancel() end
  menu.Position = CLOSED
  menu.Visible = true
  current = TweenService:Create(menu, info, {Position = OPEN})
  current:Play()
end
local function close()
  if current then current:Cancel() end
  local t = TweenService:Create(menu, info, {Position = CLOSED})
  current = t
  t.Completed:Connect(function(state)
    if state == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed and current == t then menu.Visible = false end
  end)
  t:Play()
end
```
Set AnchorPoint to (0.5, 0.5) for centring. The Completed state check makes sure that reopening during the slide-out doesn't hide the menu.
B10:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local RANGE, DAMAGE = 200, 20
local function shoot(player: Player, targetPos: Vector3)
  if typeof(targetPos) ~= 'Vector3' or targetPos ~= targetPos then return end
  local char = player.Character
  local head = char and char:FindFirstChild('Head')
  local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
  if not head or not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
  local origin = head.Position
  local offset = targetPos - origin
  if offset.Magnitude < 1e-3 then return end
  local params = RaycastParams.new()
  params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
  params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {char}
  local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, offset.Unit * RANGE, params)
  if not result then return end
  local model = result.Instance:FindFirstAncestorOfClass('Model')
  local targetHum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
  if targetHum and targetHum.Health > 0 then targetHum:TakeDamage(DAMAGE) end
end
```
The range comes from the unit direction times 200. The shooter is excluded. NaN and zero-length targets are rejected. Add a fire-rate check when this is called from a remote.

```lua
local CollectionService = game:GetService('CollectionService')
local TAG = 'KillBrick'
local conns = {} :: {[BasePart]: RBXScriptConnection}
```

B12:
```lua
local TeleportService = game:GetService('TeleportService')
local MAX, BACKOFF = 4, 2
local function safeTeleport(placeId, players, teleportData)
  local options = Instance.new('TeleportOptions')
  if teleportData then options:SetTeleportData(teleportData) end
  for attempt = 1, MAX do
    local ok, res = pcall(TeleportService.TeleportAsync, TeleportService, placeId, players, options)
    if ok then return true, res end
    warn('Teleport attempt ' .. attempt .. ' failed: ' .. tostring(res))
    task.wait(BACKOFF * attempt)
  end
  return false
end
TeleportService.TeleportInitFailed:Connect(function(player, result, msg, placeId, options)
  if result == Enum.TeleportResult.Flooded or result == Enum.TeleportResult.Failure then
    task.delay(BACKOFF, function()
      if player.Parent then pcall(TeleportService.TeleportAsync, TeleportService, placeId, {player}, options) end
    end)
  end -- for IsTeleporting/Unauthorized/GameEnded, notify the player instead of retrying
end)
return safeTeleport
```
TeleportAsync can succeed but still fail later per player, which TeleportInitFailed catches. Limit retries per player to avoid loops. Teleport data is client-visible, so don't put trusted values in it.
B13: (a) Client to server: a RemoteEvent (or a RemoteFunction InvokeServer if the client wants an immediate result) like BuyItem(itemId). The server owns the coin balance (in the session profile), looks up the price in server config, validates the type, existence, affordability and rate, then deducts and grants. (b) Server to client: replicate the balance with a server-set leaderstats IntValue, a Player attribute (the client listens with GetAttributeChangedSignal), or a RemoteEvent:FireClient(newBalance). Never let the client tell the server its balance. Avoid RemoteFunction:InvokeClient for UI updates: the server yields until the client answers, a malicious or disconnected client can hang that server thread forever or throw errors, and you gain nothing because the server doesn't need a reply. Fire-and-forget events or replicated values are safe.
B14: Teleport data (TeleportOptions:SetTeleportData) travels with the client and is readable and modifiable by an exploiter. It is only acceptable for non-authoritative hints such as the chosen loadout (validate it against what the player owns) or a match or party id. Coin balances must not travel in teleport data. DataStores are the authoritative, persistent store: do the final save with session-lock release before the teleport, and load on arrival (wait for the lock). MemoryStore (SortedMap or HashMap with a short TTL) is good for fast, short-lived cross-server handoff, such as a match roster or reserved server info, but it is not durable. Choice: coins live in the session-locked DataStore profile. The loadout is saved in the profile too, or passed in teleport data as a hint and re-validated on the server. Use MemoryStore for the matchmaking and roster handoff.
B15: Per-instance Scripts (610 copies): every copy is a separate script VM thread with duplicated code and memory. A bug fix means editing hundreds of copies, which drift apart, and startup and memory costs grow. Copies are hard to stream and pool, and duplicated connections can leak. Tag-driven approach: put a CollectionService tag on each instance ('Door', 'Pickup', 'Turret'), with per-instance settings in Attributes. Then one server Script or ModuleScript per kind, such as DoorSystem, PickupSystem and TurretSystem (plus client modules for visuals), handles them all. Each system calls GetTagged for existing instances, connects GetInstanceAddedSignal for newly spawned or streamed-in ones, and on GetInstanceRemovedSignal disconnects and clears per-instance state through a connections or Janitor table. Turrets share one Heartbeat loop over a set instead of 60 loops. Client code uses the same pattern, so StreamingEnabled is handled automatically. Make models Atomic where needed.
B16: Give the driver client network ownership of the car's assembly (VehicleSeat or the root part: part:SetNetworkOwner(driver) when they sit, and back to nil or the server when they leave). This gives responsive, lag-free physics. Risk: the owner simulates the car's physics, so an exploiter can teleport it, speed-hack, fly or fling other cars and players, and the server just accepts the physics state. The server must still validate: speed and acceleration bounds per tick, and teleport-distance checks, resetting or kicking on violation. Check that the position stays on track (no shortcuts or noclip), checkpoint order and lap times (compute the race result and finish on the server using server-side checkpoint triggers), who is seated, and all damage, boosts and purchases. Never trust client-reported race results or speed. If you need the strongest protection, Server Authority mode with prediction is the alternative.
B17: Use an UnreliableRemoteEvent for the per-tick aim and position stream. Messages are not resent or ordered, so they don't block the queue, and dropping an old aim sample is harmless. Better still, send only on change at 10-20 Hz and quantize (for example buffer-packed or compressed vectors). Constraints: delivery is not guaranteed and order is not guaranteed, so include a sequence number or timestamp and discard stale packets; each payload is limited to about 1000 bytes, larger ones are dropped, so keep it small. Never use it for important one-shot events (fire, hit, purchase); use a normal RemoteEvent for those. The server must still validate and rate-limit, clamp values, check for NaN, and interpolate between samples. Also consider whether the server needs it at all: character position already replicates, so you may only need the aim.
B18: Put the NPC logic under Actors, for example one Actor per batch of about 10-25 NPCs (not 200 single actors), each with its own script. In RunService.Heartbeat, use ConnectParallel (or task.desynchronize) to run raycasts, path scoring and target selection in parallel. Raycasts and reading the world are allowed in the desynchronized phase. Then call task.synchronize() (or post results to a serial step) to apply writes: moving parts, setting Humanoid MoveTo, changing properties and firing remotes. Limitations: in parallel you cannot write to instances outside your Actor or call most yielding or non-thread-safe APIs. Actors don't share Lua state, so share data through SharedTable or messages (Actor:SendMessage / BindToMessageParallel), which costs copies. Pathfinding ComputeAsync yields, so run it serially or less often. Results must be deterministic regardless of order. Also cut the work itself: stagger NPCs across frames, lower the rate for distant or idle NPCs, and profile with the MicroProfiler.
B19: Turn on Workspace.StreamingEnabled (set it in the Studio Properties panel; it can't be set from scripts). Sensible settings: StreamingMinRadius 64 (default), StreamingTargetRadius about 1024 (default; lower it, for example 512, for mobile-heavy games; it must be greater than the min radius), StreamOutBehavior = Opportunistic, StreamingIntegrityMode = PauseOutsideLoadedArea (or MinimumRadiusPause), ModelStreamingBehavior = Improved, and PredictiveStreaming if available. Per model: ModelStreamingMode Atomic for interactables, Nonatomic for scenery, Persistent only for small essentials, PersistentPerPlayer for a player's own base. Scripts: replace direct indexing with WaitForChild (with a timeout) on Atomic models, and drive things with CollectionService GetInstanceAddedSignal and RemovedSignal. Expect instances to stream out (disconnect and clean up). Keep state off Workspace instances and in ReplicatedStorage or attributes on Player. Call Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync before moving or teleporting players on the server. Move server-relevant logic to the server. Test with low radii on a mobile emulator.
B20: Cause: 80 players x 12 writes per minute is about 960 writes per minute, far above the experience and server write budgets (about 300 + 20 x CCU per minute experience-wide, and roughly 60 + 40 x players per server). It also hits the per-key write-rate limits. The request queues (about 30 entries) fill up and fail with error 302 (queue full), and those saves are lost. Better design: keep data in memory in a session-locked profile. Write only on join (load), autosave every 60-180 s with a random per-player offset and jitter, save on PlayerRemoving and in BindToClose, and checkpoint on purchases (with an optional debounced save soon after important events, 2-10 s debounce). Use UpdateAsync with retry and exponential backoff. Check GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before non-critical writes, skip saves when nothing changed (a dirty flag), and keep the payload small.
B21: Enable it in Studio: open the Assistant panel, open its ... menu, choose Manage MCP Servers, and turn on 'Enable Studio as MCP server'. A green indicator shows connected clients. Then add it to the client, for example in Claude Code: claude mcp add --scope user Roblox_Studio -- cmd.exe /c "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\mcp.bat" (on macOS, the equivalent mcp script), or use the JSON config or Quick connect, and restart the client. Tools it exposes include: list_roblox_studios, search_game_tree, inspect_instance, script_read, script_search, script_grep, multi_edit, execute_luau, get_studio_state, start_stop_play, get_console_output, screen_capture, character_navigation, user_keyboard_input, user_mouse_input, search_asset, insert_asset, upload_image, generate_mesh, generate_material and wait_job_finished. Call list_roblox_studios first each session (the id changes on every restart). Edit calls fail during Play.
B22: There are three core instances. InputContext is a group of actions with Enabled, Priority and Sink. InputAction is a named action with a Type: Bool, Direction1D, Direction2D, Direction3D or ViewportPosition. InputBinding is a child of the action that maps a device input: KeyCode (keyboard or gamepad), UIButton (a touch GuiButton), plus modifiers or composite directions and thresholds. Signalling: a Bool action fires Pressed and Released, any action fires StateChanged(state), and you can poll action:GetState(), which suits analog input every frame. Precedence: give the menu InputContext a higher Priority than the gameplay or default player-script contexts and set Sink = true, so the keys it binds are consumed and lower contexts never see them. Enable the menu context while the menu is open (and optionally disable the gameplay context), then disable it on close. The default player scripts move to IAS through Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem.
B23: It is the engine UI Styling system (StyleSheets). Main instances: StyleSheet (a container of rules, which can also hold tokens as attributes); StyleRule (a Selector string plus property values set with SetProperty/SetProperties, with nested rules and priority); StyleLink (connects a StyleSheet to a UI tree, usually under a ScreenGui, so its rules apply to that tree); StyleDerive (makes one sheet inherit another, for a base sheet plus themes); and StyleQuery for screen-size or input conditions. Selectors match the class (TextButton), tags (.Primary, via CollectionService tags), names (#Name), states (:hover, :pressed) and pseudo-instances (::UICorner) that add modifiers. Rules reach UI through the StyleLink and cascade over matching descendants. Tokens: define attributes on a token or theme StyleSheet (for example PrimaryColor = Color3) and reference them in rule values as "$PrimaryColor". Swapping or deriving a theme sheet with the same token names re-themes everything. Don't set the same property from code and from styles, and only one linked sheet applies per tree.
B24: Roblox requires an age check to use chat. It uses facial age estimation through the app's camera (run by the vendor Persona; images are not stored), with ID verification as an option for 13+. It rolled out from late 2025 in some countries and became global in January 2026. Players are placed in age groups: under 9, 9-12, 13-15, 16-17, 18-20 and 21+. They can chat only with players in their own group and the groups directly next to it; for example, 13-15 can chat with 9-12, 13-15 and 16-17, and under-16s cannot chat with adults. Players who have not been checked lose access to chat. Under-9s have chat off by default unless a parent consents (and Roblox Kids accounts have communication off). Trusted Connections can extend chat to people the player knows. Developers can check with TextChatService:CanUsersChatAsync, CanUsersDirectChatAsync and GetChatGroupsAsync. There is no API that exposes a player's age, and gameplay must not depend on chat.
